description: We are STEM students from Egypt passionate about space exploration, science, sustainability, and creative problem-solving. details:
Project Details – BEYOND EARTH

BEYOND EARTH is an interactive educational website developed by team ANA.NASA⁵ for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, under the challenge "Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer."

What does the project do and how does it work?

BEYOND EARTH introduces students to the challenges of exploring worlds beyond Earth through an interactive learning experience. The website features four destinations: Mars, Venus, Europa (Jupiter's moon), and Titan (Saturn's moon).

Each destination has its own dedicated page containing scientific information, NASA-based images and references, and a 10-question interactive quiz. Students can explore each world, test their knowledge, receive feedback on their answers, and learn from their mistakes.

The website also includes a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer, where students engage with space-related challenges and consider essential requirements for future missions, including oxygen and life support, water, food, energy, radiation protection, and temperature control.

What are its benefits and intended impact?

The project makes space science more accessible and engaging for students. Instead of relying only on reading and memorization, learners are encouraged to explore, interact, apply scientific knowledge, and think critically.

Our intended impact is to inspire curiosity about space exploration, strengthen problem-solving and decision-making skills, and encourage more students to pursue interests in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM).

What tools and technologies did we use?

We developed the website using:

  • HTML to structure the website and its content.
  • CSS to design the interface, layouts, animations, and visual experience.
  • JavaScript to create interactive features, quizzes, feedback, and mission activities.
  • Visual Studio Code as our development environment.
  • GitHub for code hosting and version control.
  • GitHub Pages to publish the website and make it publicly accessible.
  • NASA resources and imagery to support the scientific content.

The project is a software-based educational prototype and does not require additional physical hardware.

What makes our project creative?

Our creative approach is based on combining planetary exploration with interactive learning and mission-based thinking in one experience. We chose four different destinations with distinct environments to help students understand that every world presents unique exploration challenges.

We also designed the experience to move beyond passive learning: students explore, answer questions, receive feedback, and engage with mission-related decisions.

What factors did our team consider?

During development, we considered:

  • Scientific accuracy and the reliability of information by referring to NASA resources.
  • Ease of use and accessibility for students.
  • Clear organization of information for different planetary destinations.
  • Engagement through interactive quizzes and mission activities.
  • The educational value of connecting scientific concepts to practical challenges.
  • The importance of presenting space exploration in an exciting but scientifically responsible way.

Through BEYOND EARTH, we aim to turn curiosity about the universe into an opportunity for learning, exploration, and critical thinking.
